review_method: Pages retrieved and read with the research fetch tool. Download transport is independently recorded; GitHub mirrors are not organizer-authenticated originals.

sources.title: DrivenData: problem, metric, submission format
sources.locator: Performance metric / Mathematical representation / Submission format
sources.verified_claim: Predict fault presence as a single-band float32 GeoTIFF, values [0,1], UTM zone 11N / EPSG:32611, 100 m; use the sample grid. Distance-weighted Tversky has alpha=0.2, beta=0.8, triangular kernel support 300 m.
sources.qualification: The public wording allows null/NaN outside bounds. Our zero-filled all-finite export is a stricter local range policy, not proof of authenticated portal acceptance.

sources.title: DrivenData staff clarification: exact known-fault masking
sources.verified_claim: Pixels corresponding to known USGS/INGENIOUS faults are excluded from evaluation, including re-evaluation.
sources.qualification: This is pixel-exact masking, not permission to remove a broad halo from the scored domain.

sources.title: DrivenData: about the task and data
sources.verified_claim: Faults involve measurable displacement and can be detected with surface observations, magnetic/gravity contrasts, and other methods.
sources.qualification: A structural prediction alone does not prove a geothermal vent or commercially viable reservoir.

sources.title: DrivenData submissions and account cap

sources.title: Official GEMS reference solution
sources.retrieval: README retrieved; notebook downloaded through GitHub API at aebe92f7c8a990f0e3443451b7a825d9afd6336b
sources.verified_claim: Provides a reproducible starting approach and asks participants to place competition data in data/; GPU training is faster but CPU execution is supported.
sources.qualification: H87 is a deterministic CPU image-statistic experiment, not a claimed U-Net training run. Pinned notebook cells 0, 1 and 16 were inspected: ordinary Tversky training loss and random patch Monte Carlo CV are not substitutes for official distance-weighted evaluation or the required whole-component holdout.

sources.title: USGS GeoDAWN magnetic and radiometric survey release
sources.verified_claim: Magnetic surveys support subsurface structure and geology; the release documents east-west flight lines, north-south tie lines, survey blocks, and variable terrain clearance. Rights marked CC0 1.0.
sources.qualification: Acquisition artifacts may mimic geological texture; the original flight-line grids were not newly downloaded in this lane.

sources.title: USGS: Matching Magnetic Trends and Patterns Across the Tintina Fault
sources.authority: USGS Scientific Investigations Report 2007–5289–C, Richard W. Saltus
sources.retrieval: abstract, introduction, and methods retrieved and read
sources.verified_claim: Cutting/sliding geophysical maps to restore magnetic pattern alignment can inform fault-displacement interpretation.
sources.qualification: A different region and scale; does not validate the H87 detector or its chosen pixel shifts.

sources.title: USGS: Aeromagnetic expression of faults that offset basin fill
sources.authority: USGS publication record; Grauch, Hudson, Minor; DOI 10.1190/1.1444961
sources.verified_claim: High-resolution aeromagnetic data show expressions of faults offsetting basin fill in the Albuquerque basin; juxtaposed magnetic layers can explain the anomalies.
sources.qualification: Supports geological plausibility, not detection accuracy in GeoDAWN or a geothermal interpretation.

sources.qualification: Contextual research; no new well, vent, or chemistry data were used as H87 features.
